summary.text: Argonaut from Peiresiae near the Phylleian mount, where the Apidanus and the Enipeus meet: son of Cometes, whom Apollonius calls Asterion and Apollodorus Asterius, or, in one of Hyginus' two accounts, son of Hyperasius.

story.text: Apollonius opens his roll of the crew with him: Asterion, whom Cometes begot by the eddying Apidanus, living at Peiresiae near the Phylleian mount. Apollodorus names the same Argonaut Asterius son of Cometes, and Hyginus, giving two accounts of one Asterion, sets the second at Piresia, at the foot of Mount Phylleus, as a son of Hyperasius.
